To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed efficient radix 3 and radix 6 DIF FHT algorithms that are comparable to the existing algorithms in terms of their computational complexity.
the radix 6 DIF FHT algorithm is more efficient than the radix 4 and 8 DIF FHT algorithms and is more efficient than split radix FHT for sequence length closer to an integer multiple of 6.
we have presented new fast algorithms for the computation of the DHT for a real valued data sequence using radix 3 and radix 6 decimation techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of fast FHT algorithms based on radix 3 and radix 6 decomposition techniques.
a radix 3 and radix 6 FHT algorithm.
the development of efficient algorithms for the computation of the DHT for a real valued data sequence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radix 6 FHT algorithm is the most efficient algorithm among the algorithms presented here.
radix 3 and radix 6 DIF FHT algorithms have the potential to be more efficient than the split radix DIF FHT algorithm for a sequence length closer to an integer multiple of the corresponding radix.
the radix 6 FHT algorithm is the most efficient algorithm for a sequence length of 6n.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithms can be used for the computation of DHT for real valued sequences.
the radix 6 FHT algorithm has the lowest operation count for the sequence length N = 3 ^{k} and the radix 3 FHT algorithm has a better operation count for the remaining sequence lengths.
we have presented efficient radix 3 and radix 6 FHTs which are comparable to the existing radix 2, 4, and split radix algorithms in terms of the number of complex multiplications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radix 6 decimation-in-frequency FHT algorithm has an operation count of approximately 1.5 times that of the corresponding radix 3 DIF FHT algorithm.

the decomposition technique used for the radix 3 DIF FHT algorithm can also be used for the radix-6 DIF FHT algorithms and the operation count can be further reduced by using a suitable reordering of the sequence.
the DIF FHT algorithms can be efficiently implemented by applying the decomposition techniques of the DIF FFT algorithms.
